cards.name: Squamous part of temporal bone
cards.function: Thin, fan-shaped plate forming the lower lateral wall of the cranial vault and part of the middle cranial fossa; it carries the zygomatic process and the socket of the temporomandibular joint.

details.label: Location
details.value: Side of the skull above the external acoustic meatus, overlapped by the parietal bone at the squamous suture and meeting the greater wing of the sphenoid in front

details.label: Key features
details.value: Zygomatic process, articular tubercle, mandibular fossa, supramastoid crest, groove for the posterior deep temporal artery; inner surface grooved by the middle meningeal vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis (floor of the temporal fossa), temporal fascia (supramastoid crest and zygomatic process), masseter (zygomatic process), capsule and lateral ligament of the TMJ (articular tubercle)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Temporal lobe and middle meningeal vessels medially; superficial temporal vessels and auriculotemporal nerve laterally

cards.pearl: A blow to the thin squamous temporal bone can tear the middle meningeal artery and cause an epidural hematoma: lucid interval, then a lens-shaped bleed on CT.

cards.name: Petrous part of temporal bone
cards.function: Dense pyramid of bone wedged between the sphenoid and occipital bones in the skull base; it houses the inner ear, the facial canal and the carotid canal, and its ridge separates the middle from the posterior cranial fossa. The mastoid process is its postnatal downgrowth.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs anteromedially from the mastoid region to the foramen lacerum; anterior surface in the middle cranial fossa, posterior surface in the posterior cranial fossa, inferior surface on the external cranial base

details.label: Key features
details.value: Arcuate eminence, trigeminal impression, grooves for the greater and lesser petrosal nerves, groove for the superior petrosal sinus along its ridge, internal acoustic meatus, opening of the vestibular aqueduct, groove for the sigmoid sinus, jugular fossa, external opening of the carotid canal, mastoid process and mastoid notch, groove for the occipital artery

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus – CN VII, CN VIII, labyrinthine artery; carotid canal – internal carotid artery and plexus; stylomastoid foramen – CN VII; mastoid canaliculus – auricular branch of CN X; inferior tympanic canaliculus – tympanic nerve (CN IX)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli (petrous ridge), levator veli palatini (inferior surface), cartilage of the auditory tube (groove between petrous part and greater wing)

cards.pearl: Petrous apicitis complicating otitis media gives Gradenigo syndrome: ear discharge, deep facial (trigeminal) pain and abducens palsy.

cards.name: Tympanic part of temporal bone
cards.function: Curved plate of bone below the squamous part that forms the anterior wall, floor and part of the posterior wall of the bony external acoustic meatus and sheathes the root of the styloid process.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the mandibular fossa in front and the mastoid process behind; separated from the mandibular fossa by the petrotympanic fissure

details.label: Key features
details.value: Bony external acoustic meatus; tympanic sulcus for the tympanic membrane; at birth it is only an incomplete ring, so the bony meatus is absent and the tympanic membrane lies near the surface

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Petrotympanic fissure – chorda tympani and anterior tympanic artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Head of the mandible and parotid gland anteriorly; styloid process and stylomastoid foramen (CN VII) posteroinferiorly

cards.pearl: In the newborn the bony meatus and mastoid process are absent, so the facial nerve leaves the stylomastoid foramen close to the surface and can be injured by forceps or a postauricular incision.

cards.name: Greater wing of sphenoid bone
cards.function: Large lateral wing of the sphenoid that forms the floor of the middle cranial fossa, the lateral wall of the orbit and the roof of the infratemporal fossa; it transmits the maxillary and mandibular nerves and the middle meningeal artery.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Cerebral surface (middle cranial fossa, temporal lobe); orbital surface (lateral wall of orbit); temporal surface (temporal fossa, pterion); infratemporal surface below the infratemporal crest (roof of infratemporal fossa); spine of the sphenoid posteriorly

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Foramen rotundum – V2; foramen ovale – V3, accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve; foramen spinosum – middle meningeal vessels and meningeal branch of V3; sphenoidal emissary foramen (inconstant)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis (temporal surface), upper head of lateral pterygoid (infratemporal surface and crest), sphenomandibular ligament and tensor veli palatini (spine)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Bounds the superior orbital fissure (with the lesser wing) and the inferior orbital fissure (with the maxilla); meets frontal, parietal and temporal bones at the pterion

cards.pearl: The greater wing is the thin floor of the pterion: fracture here tears the frontal branch of the middle meningeal artery and causes an epidural hematoma.

cards.name: Lesser wing of sphenoid bone
cards.function: Thin triangular plate projecting laterally from the front of the sphenoid body; it forms the posterior edge of the anterior cranial fossa and the roof of the orbital apex, and encloses the optic canal.

details.label: Location
details.value: Above the superior orbital fissure, between the orbital part of the frontal bone in front and the greater wing below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior clinoid process at its medial end; optic canal between its two roots; orbital surface forming the posterior orbital roof; sharp posterior border (sphenoid ridge) fitting the lateral sulcus of the brain

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Optic canal – optic nerve (CN II) and ophthalmic artery; superior orbital fissure (between lesser and greater wings) – CN III, IV, VI, branches of V1, superior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Free edge of the tentorium cerebelli (anterior clinoid process); levator palpebrae superioris and the common tendinous ring near the optic canal

cards.pearl: A sphenoid wing meningioma causes painless proptosis and progressive visual loss by narrowing the optic canal and superior orbital fissure.

cards.name: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid bone
cards.function: Thin midline plate hanging from the cribriform plate that forms the upper part of the bony nasal septum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline of the nasal cavity, continuous above with the crista galli

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal bone (nasal spine) and nasal bones in front, crest and body of the sphenoid behind, vomer posteroinferiorly, septal nasal cartilage anteroinferiorly

details.label: Key features
details.value: Upper edge grooved by olfactory nerve filaments descending from the cribriform plate

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory mucosa on its upper part; anterior ethmoidal nerve and vessels and the posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery supply its mucosa

cards.pearl: Twisting the perpendicular plate during septal surgery or nasal trauma can crack the cribriform plate and cause CSF rhinorrhea and anosmia.

cards.name: Orbital plate of ethmoid bone (lamina papyracea)
cards.function: Paper-thin lateral wall of the ethmoidal labyrinth that forms most of the medial wall of the orbit and separates the orbit from the ethmoidal cells.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial orbital wall, between the lacrimal bone in front and the body of the sphenoid behind, below the orbital part of the frontal bone and above the orbital surface of the maxilla

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Anterior and posterior ethmoidal foramina in the fronto-ethmoidal suture – anterior and posterior ethmoidal nerves and vessels

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thinnest wall of the orbit; ethmoidal cells lie directly behind it

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medial rectus and superior oblique laterally; ethmoidal cells medially; optic canal just behind the posterior ethmoidal foramen

cards.pearl: Ethmoid sinusitis spreads through the orbital plate to cause orbital cellulitis, and a medial-wall blowout fracture lets air into the orbit (orbital emphysema after nose blowing).

cards.name: Superior and middle nasal conchae (and highest nasal concha)
cards.function: Scroll-like projections of the ethmoidal labyrinth on the lateral nasal wall that increase mucosal surface area and roof the superior and middle meatuses; unlike the inferior concha they are parts of the ethmoid bone, not separate bones.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Highest nasal concha (inconstant, above the superior); superior nasal concha (roofs the superior meatus, sphenoethmoidal recess above it); middle nasal concha (roofs the middle meatus, covers the ethmoidal bulla, uncinate process and semilunar hiatus)

details.label: Location
details.value: Upper lateral wall of the nasal cavity, above the inferior nasal concha and below the cribriform plate

details.label: Key features
details.value: Superior meatus receives the posterior ethmoidal cells; middle meatus receives the frontal sinus, anterior and middle ethmoidal cells and maxillary sinus; sphenopalatine foramen opens behind the middle concha

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory mucosa covers the superior concha; posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery and of V2 supply the conchae

cards.pearl: A pneumatized middle concha (concha bullosa) or nasal polyps arising from the middle meatus block the osteomeatal unit and cause recurrent frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoid sinusitis.

cards.name: Alveolar process of maxilla
cards.function: Thick horseshoe-shaped ridge of the maxilla that carries the sockets of the upper teeth and forms the floor of the maxillary sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior border of the body of the maxilla, from the intermaxillary suture to the tuberosity of the maxilla behind the last molar

details.label: Key features
details.value: Sockets for the 16 upper teeth; tuberosity of the maxilla with the posterior superior alveolar foramina on the infratemporal surface above it; roots of the molars and premolars project toward the maxillary sinus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior, middle and posterior superior alveolar nerves (V2) to the teeth; buccal gingiva by the superior alveolar and infraorbital nerves, palatal gingiva by the greater palatine and nasopalatine nerves

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Buccinator (outer surface opposite the molars), upper lip muscles near the incisive fossa

cards.pearl: Extraction of an upper molar can open the sinus floor and leave an oroantral fistula; upper molar root infection is the usual cause of unilateral odontogenic maxillary sinusitis.

cards.name: Frontal process of maxilla
cards.function: Strong upward projection of the maxilla between the nasal and lacrimal bones; it forms the medial orbital margin and the side of the bony nose.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial to the orbit, lateral to the nasal bone

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal bone above, nasal bone in front, lacrimal bone behind

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior lacrimal crest bounding the fossa for the lacrimal sac in front; forms part of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity (agger nasi region)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Medial palpebral ligament and orbicularis oculi (anterior lacrimal crest), levator labii superioris alaeque nasi

cards.pearl: Naso-orbito-ethmoid fractures detach the fragment of the frontal process bearing the medial palpebral ligament, producing telecanthus and nasolacrimal obstruction.

cards.name: Zygomatic process of maxilla
cards.function: Short, stout lateral projection of the maxilla that joins the zygomatic bone and transmits chewing forces from the molars to the cheek buttress.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral side of the body of the maxilla above the first molar, separating its anterior and infratemporal surfaces

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Maxillary process of the zygomatic bone (zygomaticomaxillary suture)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Forms the lateral part of the infraorbital margin and the zygomatic recess of the maxillary sinus extends into it

details.label: Relations
details.value: Infraorbital foramen medially; masseter and zygomaticus muscles arise just lateral on the zygomatic bone

cards.pearl: The zygomaticomaxillary suture is one of the fracture lines of the zygomaticomaxillary complex (tripod) fracture, which often injures the infraorbital nerve and numbs the cheek and upper lip.

cards.name: Palatine process of maxilla
cards.function: Horizontal shelf of the maxilla that meets its fellow in the midline to form the anterior three-quarters of the hard palate and the floor of the nasal cavity.

details.label: Location
details.value: Projects medially from the body of the maxilla above the alveolar process; joins the opposite process at the intermaxillary suture and the horizontal plate of the palatine bone at the palatomaxillary suture

details.label: Key features
details.value: Incisive fossa and incisive canal behind the central incisors; nasal crest on its upper surface for the vomer, ending in front as the anterior nasal spine

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Incisive canal – nasopalatine nerve and the terminal branch of the greater palatine artery meeting the posterior septal branch of the sphenopalatine artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Greater palatine nerve and vessels run forward in a groove on its oral surface; inferior nasal meatus above

cards.pearl: Failure of the palatine shelves to fuse with each other and with the primary palate produces cleft palate, with feeding difficulty, nasal speech and recurrent otitis media.

cards.name: Horizontal plate of palatine bone
cards.function: Flat plate of the palatine bone forming the posterior quarter of the hard palate and the back of the nasal floor; its free posterior edge anchors the soft palate.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the palatine process of the maxilla (palatomaxillary suture), meeting the opposite plate in the midline

details.label: Key features
details.value: Posterior nasal spine in the midline; nasal crest on the upper surface for the vomer; greater palatine foramen at its lateral edge, lesser palatine foramina just behind in the pyramidal process

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Greater palatine foramen – greater palatine nerve and vessels; lesser palatine foramina – lesser palatine nerves and vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Palatine aponeurosis (posterior border), musculus uvulae (posterior nasal spine)

cards.pearl: A greater palatine nerve block is placed at the greater palatine foramen, medial to the upper second or third molar at the lateral edge of the horizontal plate.

cards.name: Perpendicular plate of palatine bone
cards.function: Thin vertical plate of the palatine bone forming the posterior part of the lateral nasal wall and the medial wall of the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Orbital process (upper anterior; reaches the orbital floor); sphenoidal process (upper posterior; under the body of the sphenoid); the notch between them is closed by the sphenoid to form the sphenopalatine foramen; pyramidal process at its junction with the horizontal plate

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the maxilla in front and the medial pterygoid plate behind

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Sphenopalatine foramen – sphenopalatine artery and posterior superior nasal nerves; greater palatine canal (with the maxilla) – greater and lesser palatine nerves and descending palatine vessels

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pterygopalatine ganglion and maxillary artery on its lateral side; middle and inferior nasal conchae attach to its medial surface

cards.pearl: The sphenopalatine artery crosses the top of this plate into the nose; endoscopic ligation at the sphenopalatine foramen controls refractory posterior epistaxis.

cards.name: Permanent teeth (dental arches)
cards.function: Thirty-two teeth set in the alveolar processes of the maxillae and mandible, eight per quadrant; they cut, tear and grind food and are supplied by the alveolar branches of the maxillary and mandibular nerves.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Per quadrant, from the midline: central incisor, lateral incisor, canine, 1st and 2nd premolars, 1st, 2nd and 3rd molars. Parts of each tooth: crown, neck, root. Tissues: enamel, dentine, dental pulp, cement, periodontium

details.label: Key features
details.value: Deciduous dentition has 20 teeth (two incisors, one canine, two molars per quadrant); first permanent tooth is the 1st molar in the 6th year, last the 3rd molar at 17–25 years; root canals open at apical foramina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper teeth: anterior, middle and posterior superior alveolar nerves (V2); lower teeth: inferior alveolar nerve (V3) and its incisive branch

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior alveolar arteries (posterior from the maxillary, anterior and middle from the infraorbital) and inferior alveolar artery

cards.pearl: Dental caries reaching the pulp causes pulpitis and then a periapical abscess; lower molar infections can track below the mylohyoid line into the submandibular space (Ludwig angina).

cards.name: Incisors (central and lateral)
cards.function: Chisel-edged front teeth, two per quadrant, with a single root; they cut food and support the lips for speech.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Central (medial) incisor; lateral incisor; four upper (maxillary) and four lower (mandibular)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Single conical root; permanent central incisors erupt in the 7th year and lateral incisors in the 8th; deciduous lower central incisors are the first teeth to appear, at 6–9 months

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: anterior superior alveolar nerve (V2), palatal gingiva by the nasopalatine nerve; lower: incisive branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (V3), labial gingiva by the mental nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Incisive fossa lies behind the upper central incisors; mental spines lie behind the lower incisors

cards.pearl: Notched, peg-shaped permanent incisors (Hutchinson teeth) are a late sign of congenital syphilis; an avulsed permanent incisor should be replanted within the hour.

cards.name: Canines (cuspids)
cards.function: Single pointed tooth at each corner of the dental arch with the longest root of any tooth; it pierces and tears food and guides the jaw in lateral movement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Third tooth from the midline in each quadrant, between the lateral incisor and the 1st premolar

details.label: Key features
details.value: Single cusp and one long root raising the canine eminence on the alveolar process; permanent canines erupt in the 11th–12th year, deciduous canines at 16–20 months

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: anterior superior alveolar nerve (V2); lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Root of the upper canine reaches toward the canine fossa below the infraorbital foramen; levator anguli oris arises above it

cards.pearl: The upper canine is, after the third molars, the most commonly impacted tooth; infection from its long root can spread to the canine space and present as swelling beside the nose that closes the eye.

cards.name: Premolars (1st and 2nd)
cards.function: Two bicuspid teeth in each quadrant between the canine and the molars; they crush food and have no deciduous predecessors of the same form, replacing the deciduous molars.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: 1st premolar; 2nd premolar; upper and lower in each quadrant

details.label: Key features
details.value: Two cusps; usually one root (upper 1st premolar often two); erupt in the 9th year (1st) and 10th year (2nd)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: middle superior alveolar nerve (V2), sometimes posterior or anterior when it is absent; lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mental foramen lies below the lower 2nd premolar; roots of the upper premolars lie close to the floor of the maxillary sinus

cards.pearl: The mental foramen below the lower second premolar is the landmark for a mental nerve block and must be protected when plating a mandibular body fracture.

cards.name: Molars (1st, 2nd and 3rd)
cards.function: Three broad multi-cusped grinding teeth at the back of each quadrant; the first is the earliest permanent tooth and the third (wisdom tooth) the last and most variable.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: 1st molar (6th year); 2nd molar (12th–13th year); 3rd molar (17th–25th year); upper molars usually have three roots, lower molars two

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior alveolar process, the upper molars below the maxillary sinus and in front of the tuberosity of the maxilla, the lower molars in front of the retromolar fossa

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: posterior superior alveolar nerve (V2), with the middle superior alveolar nerve to part of the 1st molar; lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3); buccal gingiva of the lower molars by the buccal nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid duct opens opposite the upper 2nd molar; lingual nerve lies against the mandible beside the lower 3rd molar; roots of the lower 2nd and 3rd molars lie below the mylohyoid line

cards.pearl: Lower third molar extraction endangers the lingual nerve (loss of taste and sensation on the anterior tongue) and the inferior alveolar nerve; infection from lower molar roots spreads to the submandibular space.

cards.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint
cards.function: Oval fibrocartilage plate between the head of the mandible and the temporal bone that divides the joint into an upper gliding compartment and a lower hinge compartment.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle above and the head of the condylar process below, fused to the joint capsule at its edges

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thin avascular centre with thicker anterior and posterior bands; slides forward with the condyle onto the articular tubercle when the jaws open widely

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Joint capsule all round; upper head of lateral pterygoid anteriorly; vascular retrodiscal tissue posteriorly

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve (V3) to the capsule and periphery of the disc

cards.pearl: Anterior disc displacement gives a click on opening when the disc reduces, and a painful closed lock with limited opening when it does not.

cards.name: Joint capsule and lateral ligament of temporomandibular joint
cards.function: Loose fibrous capsule enclosing the temporomandibular joint, thickened on its outer side as the lateral ligament, the only true ligament of the joint, which prevents backward displacement of the condyle.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Capsule: margins of the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle above, neck of the mandible below. Lateral ligament: articular tubercle and root of the zygomatic process, running down and back to the lateral and posterior neck of the mandible

details.label: Key features
details.value: Capsule is lax above the disc (gliding) and tight below it (hinge); the lateral ligament limits posterior and inferior movement of the condyle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve, with twigs from the masseteric and deep temporal nerves (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland, superficial temporal vessels and auriculotemporal nerve behind; temporal and zygomatic branches of CN VII cross lateral to it

cards.pearl: Because the capsule is weakest in front, the condyle dislocates anteriorly over the articular tubercle with a wide yawn and the jaw locks open.

cards.name: Sphenomandibular ligament
cards.function: Flat band from the spine of the sphenoid to the lingula of the mandible, a remnant of the first-arch (Meckel) cartilage; it is the pivot about which the mandible swings and the medial guide for the inferior alveolar nerve.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Spine of the sphenoid bone above; lingula and lower margin of the mandibular foramen below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Stays equally taut throughout opening and closing, so the mandible rotates about an axis near the mandibular foramen

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior alveolar nerve and vessels pass between it and the ramus to enter the mandibular foramen; maxillary artery and auriculotemporal nerve pass between it and the neck of the mandible; lingual nerve, medial pterygoid and chorda tympani lie medial; the mylohyoid nerve and vessels pierce it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Perichondrium of Meckel cartilage (first pharyngeal arch)

cards.pearl: For an inferior alveolar nerve block the anesthetic is placed in the pterygomandibular space lateral to this ligament, just above the lingula.

cards.name: Stylomandibular ligament
cards.function: Thickened band of the deep cervical fascia running from the styloid process to the angle of the mandible; it separates the parotid from the submandibular gland and limits excessive protrusion of the jaw.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tip of the styloid process above; angle and posterior border of the ramus of the mandible below

details.label: Key features
details.value: A specialization of the parotid sheath (investing layer of deep cervical fascia) rather than a true joint ligament; slack when the jaws are closed, taut on protrusion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland in front and above, submandibular gland below and medial; external carotid artery passes deep to it to enter the parotid

details.label: Function
details.value: Accessory ligament of the temporomandibular joint

cards.name: Stylohyoid ligament
cards.function: Fibrous cord from the tip of the styloid process to the lesser horn of the hyoid, a second-arch derivative that suspends the hyoid from the skull base.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tip of the styloid process above; lesser horn of the hyoid bone below; the middle pharyngeal constrictor arises from its lower end

details.label: Key features
details.value: May be partly or completely ossified

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the external and internal carotid arteries; glossopharyngeal nerve and stylopharyngeus pass deep to it toward the pharynx; lingual artery and hypoglossal nerve cross below it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Second pharyngeal arch (Reichert) cartilage, with the styloid process, stapes and lesser horn of the hyoid

cards.pearl: A calcified stylohyoid ligament or elongated styloid process causes Eagle syndrome: throat and ear pain on swallowing or turning the head.

cards.name: Body of hyoid bone
cards.function: Central quadrilateral bar of the hyoid lying at the C3 level; it anchors the floor of the mouth and tongue above and the infrahyoid strap muscles below.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline of the anterior neck between the chin and the laryngeal prominence, joined to the greater and lesser horns at each end

details.label: Attachments (suprahyoid)
details.value: Geniohyoid and mylohyoid (anterior surface), genioglossus (lowest fibres), hyoglossus (lateral part), fibrous loop for the intermediate tendon of digastric and insertion of stylohyoid (junction with the greater horn)

details.label: Attachments (infrahyoid)
details.value: Sternohyoid (medial lower border), omohyoid (lateral lower border), thyrohyoid (with the greater horn); thyrohyoid membrane and hyoepiglottic ligament (posterior surface)

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Upper part from the second arch, lower part from the third arch

cards.pearl: A thyroglossal duct cyst is tethered to the body of the hyoid and rises with tongue protrusion; the Sistrunk operation removes the central body with the cyst to prevent recurrence.

cards.name: Greater horn of hyoid bone
cards.function: Long posterior limb of the hyoid projecting back from each end of the body; it is the palpable lateral landmark of the hyoid and a key guide to the lingual artery and superior laryngeal nerve.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs posterosuperiorly from the body at the C3 level, ending in a tubercle that gives attachment to the lateral thyrohyoid ligament

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Hyoglossus (upper surface), middle pharyngeal constrictor (upper border), thyrohyoid (lower border), thyrohyoid membrane and lateral thyrohyoid ligament (tip)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingual artery loops above it and passes deep to hyoglossus; hypoglossal nerve crosses superficial to hyoglossus just above it; internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve pierces the thyrohyoid membrane just below it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Third pharyngeal arch

cards.pearl: Fracture of a greater horn in an adult strongly suggests manual strangulation; the tip of the horn is the landmark for a superior laryngeal nerve block.

cards.name: Lesser horn of hyoid bone
cards.function: Small conical projection at the junction of the body and greater horn of the hyoid that receives the stylohyoid ligament.

details.label: Location
details.value: Projects upward and backward from the body–greater horn junction

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Stylohyoid ligament (tip), middle pharyngeal constrictor (with the greater horn and the ligament)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Joined to the body by fibrous tissue, often by a small synovial joint, and may remain cartilaginous into adult life

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Second pharyngeal arch (Reichert cartilage), with the stylohyoid ligament and styloid process

cards.name: Lamina of thyroid cartilage
cards.function: One of the two quadrilateral plates of the thyroid cartilage that meet in the midline at the laryngeal prominence and shield the vocal folds.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterolateral wall of the larynx at C4–C5; the two laminae fuse anteriorly below the superior thyroid notch and are open posteriorly

details.label: Key features
details.value: Oblique line on the outer surface; laryngeal prominence and superior thyroid notch in the midline; posterior border prolonged into the superior and inferior horns; the angle between the laminae is more acute in men

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and the thyropharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor (oblique line); thyrohyoid membrane (upper border); cricothyroid (lower border and inferior horn); thyroepiglottic ligament, vocal ligaments, thyroarytenoid and vocalis (inner surface near the midline)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lobes of the thyroid gland and the superior thyroid vessels lie on its outer surface; piriform recess lies between its inner surface and the aryepiglottic fold

cards.pearl: The vocal folds attach to the inner midline of the laminae about halfway down, so a blow that fractures the thyroid cartilage produces hoarseness, subcutaneous emphysema and airway compromise.

cards.name: Superior and inferior horns of thyroid cartilage
cards.function: Upward and downward prolongations of the posterior border of each thyroid lamina; the superior horn suspends the larynx from the hyoid and the inferior horn forms the cricothyroid joint.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior horn (long; joined to the tip of the greater horn of the hyoid by the lateral thyrohyoid ligament, which contains the triticeal cartilage); inferior horn (short; medial facet articulates with the side of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Lateral thyrohyoid ligament and stylopharyngeus/palatopharyngeus fibres (posterior border and superior horn); cricothyroid muscle (inferior horn)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve enters the larynx immediately behind the cricothyroid joint, deep to the lower border of the inferior constrictor; superior laryngeal vessels and internal laryngeal nerve pierce the thyrohyoid membrane in front of the superior horn

details.label: Movements
details.value: At the cricothyroid joints the thyroid cartilage tilts forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments

cards.pearl: The inferior horn is the surgical landmark for the recurrent laryngeal nerve, which enters the larynx just behind the cricothyroid joint and is most at risk there during thyroidectomy.

cards.name: Arch of cricoid cartilage
cards.function: Narrow anterior band of the signet-ring-shaped cricoid, palpable below the laryngeal prominence at C6; it is the lower boundary of the cricothyroid interval used for emergency airway access.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior and lateral part of the cricoid, between the median cricothyroid ligament above and the first tracheal ring below

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Median cricothyroid ligament and conus elasticus (upper border), cricothyroid muscle (outer surface), cricotracheal ligament (lower border), cricopharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor (side)

details.label: Key features
details.value: 5–7 mm tall in front, deepening posteriorly toward the lamina; bears a facet on each side for the inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Isthmus of the thyroid gland lies just below it over the 2nd–4th tracheal rings

cards.pearl: In cricothyrotomy the airway is entered through the median cricothyroid ligament just above the cricoid arch; in children under about 8 years the cricoid ring is the narrowest part of the airway.

cards.name: Lamina of cricoid cartilage
cards.function: Broad quadrilateral posterior plate of the cricoid that carries the arytenoid cartilages and forms the rigid back wall of the lower larynx.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior larynx at C6, between the thyroid laminae, directly in front of the laryngopharynx and the start of the esophagus

details.label: Key features
details.value: Arytenoid articular surfaces on the sloping upper border; median ridge on the posterior surface with a depression on each side

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscles (posterior surface depressions), longitudinal muscle of the esophagus by the cricoesophageal tendon (median ridge), capsules of the cricoarytenoid joints

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerves ascend on each side behind the cricothyroid joints; cricopharyngeus encircles the pharyngoesophageal junction behind it

cards.pearl: Backward pressure on the cricoid (Sellick maneuver) uses the complete ring and broad lamina to compress the esophagus against the C6 vertebral body.

cards.name: Anterior arch of atlas
cards.function: Short curved bar joining the two lateral masses of the atlas in front; it articulates with the dens to form the front of the median atlanto-axial pivot joint.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior tubercle in the midline; articular facet for the dens on its posterior surface

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Anterior articular facet of the dens (median atlanto-axial joint)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Anterior longitudinal ligament and longus colli (anterior tubercle), anterior atlanto-occipital membrane (upper border)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nasopharynx and prevertebral muscles in front; dens and transverse ligament of the atlas behind

cards.pearl: On a lateral cervical film the gap between the anterior arch and the dens should not exceed 3 mm in adults (5 mm in children); widening means transverse ligament laxity or rupture, as in rheumatoid arthritis or Down syndrome.

cards.name: Posterior arch of atlas
cards.function: Longer curved bar joining the lateral masses of the atlas behind; it replaces a spinous process with a small tubercle and is grooved above by the vertebral artery.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Posterior tubercle in the midline; groove for the vertebral artery on the upper surface just behind each lateral mass

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Rectus capitis posterior minor and nuchal ligament (posterior tubercle), posterior atlanto-occipital membrane (upper border)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery and the C1 (suboccipital) nerve lie in the groove, in the floor of the suboccipital triangle; the C2 nerve emerges below the arch

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: None directly; bounds the vertebral foramen behind the spinal cord

cards.pearl: The vertebral artery on the posterior arch is at risk in suboccipital surgery and in posterior C1 fixation; a bony bridge over the groove (arcuate foramen) is a common variant.

cards.name: Lateral mass of atlas
cards.function: Thick weight-bearing pillar on each side of the atlas that transmits the weight of the head from the occipital condyle to the axis.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Concave, kidney-shaped superior articular surface for the occipital condyle; flat circular inferior articular surface for the axis; tubercle for the transverse ligament of the atlas on its medial side; transverse process with transverse foramen projecting laterally

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Occipital condyle (atlanto-occipital joint: flexion–extension) and superior articular facet of the axis (lateral atlanto-axial joint: rotation)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Transverse ligament of the atlas (medial tubercle); rectus capitis anterior (front); rectus capitis lateralis, obliquus capitis superior and inferior, levator scapulae and splenius cervicis (transverse process)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery ascends through the transverse foramen and turns medially behind the lateral mass; C1 anterior ramus passes round its lateral side

cards.pearl: Axial loading (diving) bursts the atlas ring at its thin arches (Jefferson fracture); on an open-mouth view the lateral masses overhang the axis, and combined overhang over 7 mm implies transverse ligament rupture.

cards.name: Dens (odontoid process) of axis
cards.function: Tooth-like peg projecting up from the body of the axis; it represents the body of the atlas and is the pivot around which the atlas and head rotate.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior articular facet for the anterior arch of the atlas; posterior articular facet for the transverse ligament of the atlas; pointed apex

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Anterior arch of the atlas in front and transverse ligament behind (median atlanto-axial joint)

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Apical ligament (apex to the anterior margin of the foramen magnum), alar ligaments (sides of the dens to the occipital condyles), cruciate ligament behind, tectorial membrane behind that

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the anterior third of the atlas ring with the spinal cord occupying the middle third; medulla and upper cord immediately behind

cards.pearl: Dens fractures follow falls in the elderly; a fracture through its base (type II) has a poor blood supply and often fails to unite, and posterior displacement threatens the cord.

cards.name: Cervical vertebral arch (pedicles, laminae, spinous process)
cards.function: Bony ring behind the vertebral body that encloses the large triangular vertebral foramen and protects the cervical enlargement of the spinal cord.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Pedicle (short, joins body to the articular pillar; forms roof and floor of the intervertebral foramina); lamina (thin plate from articular pillar to the midline); spinous process (short and bifid at C2–C6, long and non-bifid at C7)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Vertebral foramen is large and triangular in the cervical region; superior and inferior vertebral notches on the pedicles

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Ligamenta flava (laminae); nuchal ligament and interspinous ligaments (spinous processes); semispinalis cervicis, multifidus, spinalis and interspinales (spinous processes)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Spinal cord and meninges within; spinal nerves leave above the pedicle of the same-numbered vertebra (C8 below C7)

cards.pearl: A clay-shoveler fracture is an avulsion of the C7 (or C6) spinous process; decompressive laminectomy removes the laminae and spinous processes for cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

cards.name: Cervical articular processes and facet (zygapophysial) joints
cards.function: Superior and inferior articular processes form a column (articular pillar) at the junction of pedicle and lamina on each side; their flat oblique facets make the synovial zygapophysial joints that guide neck movement.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior articular process and facet (faces up and back); inferior articular process and facet (faces down and forward)

details.label: Location
details.value: From C2–C3 down to C7–T1, behind the transverse processes; the C1–C2 lateral atlanto-axial joints lie further forward

details.label: Key features
details.value: Facets slope about 45 degrees, permitting flexion, extension, lateral flexion and rotation; each joint forms the posterior wall of an intervertebral foramen

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Medial branches of the posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves

cards.pearl: Flexion–rotation injury can lock an inferior facet in front of the one below (jumped facet); unilateral dislocation shifts the body less than half its width, bilateral dislocation more than half and usually damages the cord.

cards.name: Cervical transverse process (anterior and posterior tubercles)
cards.function: Short lateral process of a cervical vertebra pierced by the transverse foramen; its two tubercles anchor the scalene and prevertebral muscles and its gutter carries the emerging spinal nerve.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior tubercle (costal element; largest at C6 as the carotid tubercle, inconspicuous at C7); posterior tubercle (true transverse element); costal lamella joining them in front of the groove; groove for the spinal nerve; transverse foramen medially

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Anterior tubercles: scalenus anterior, longus capitis, longus colli; posterior tubercles: scalenus medius and posterior, levator scapulae, splenius cervicis, longissimus and iliocostalis cervicis

details.label: Contents
details.value: Transverse foramen – vertebral artery (C6 upward), vertebral veins and sympathetic plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior ramus of the spinal nerve passes laterally behind the vertebral artery in the groove; roots of the brachial plexus emerge between the tubercles, between scalenus anterior and medius

cards.pearl: An enlarged costal element of C7 forms a cervical rib, which can compress the lower trunk of the brachial plexus and the subclavian artery (thoracic outlet syndrome).

cards.name: Cervical intervertebral discs (anulus fibrosus and nucleus pulposus)
cards.function: Fibrocartilaginous joints between adjacent vertebral bodies from C2–C3 to C7–T1; they bear load, absorb shock and allow movement. There is no disc between the occiput and atlas or between the atlas and axis.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anulus fibrosus (outer concentric lamellae of fibrocartilage binding the bodies); nucleus pulposus (gelatinous core, remnant of the notochord)

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the vertebral bodies of C2–C3, C3–C4, C4–C5, C5–C6, C6–C7 and C7–T1; thicker in front, contributing to cervical lordosis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Uncovertebral joints at the posterolateral margins; anterior longitudinal ligament in front; posterior longitudinal ligament and spinal cord behind; intervertebral foramen and spinal nerve posterolaterally

details.label: Key features
details.value: Avascular in the adult, nourished by diffusion through the vertebral end plates; only the outer anulus is innervated

cards.pearl: Cervical disc herniation is most common at C5–C6 and C6–C7 and compresses the root numbered for the lower vertebra (C6 and C7 respectively); central herniation causes myelopathy.

cards.name: T1 vertebra
cards.function: First thoracic vertebra, transitional between the neck and thorax; it carries the first rib, forms the back of the thoracic inlet and its spine is usually as prominent as that of C7.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Body (cervical-like, with uncinate processes; complete superior costal facet for the head of the 1st rib and an inferior demifacet for the 2nd); pedicles; laminae; transverse processes with transverse costal facets for the tubercle of the 1st rib; superior and inferior articular processes; long, nearly horizontal spinous process

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: C7 above and T2 below (discs and facet joints); head and tubercle of the 1st rib

details.label: Relations
details.value: Stellate (cervicothoracic) ganglion lies in front of the neck of the 1st rib beside the body; T1 anterior ramus crosses the neck of the 1st rib to join the brachial plexus; apex of the lung and subclavian vessels anterolaterally

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Longus colli (body); trapezius, rhomboid minor, serratus posterior superior and splenius (spinous process)

cards.pearl: An apical (Pancoast) lung tumor invades the structures beside T1, giving shoulder and ulnar-side arm pain from the lower trunk and Horner syndrome from the stellate ganglion.

cards.name: Clavicle
cards.function: S-shaped strut connecting the sternum to the scapula; it forms the anterior boundary of the root of the neck and the base of the posterior triangle and gives origin to sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Sternal (medial) end – sternoclavicular joint; shaft – medial two-thirds convex forward, lateral third concave forward; acromial (lateral) end – acromioclavicular joint

details.label: Location
details.value: Subcutaneous along its whole length at the junction of neck and thorax, above the 1st rib

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Clavicular head of sternocleidomastoid (upper surface of the medial third), sternohyoid (medial end), trapezius (lateral third), subclavius (inferior surface of the middle third), investing layer of deep cervical fascia and the omohyoid fascial sling; pectoralis major and deltoid in front

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subclavian vessels and trunks of the brachial plexus pass behind its middle third; supraclavicular nerves cross it; external jugular vein pierces the fascia just above it

cards.pearl: The clavicle usually fractures at the junction of its middle and lateral thirds: sternocleidomastoid pulls the medial fragment up while the arm's weight drops the lateral fragment; subclavius protects the subclavian vessels.
